research_mode: official Environment Agency, Met Office and UK Health Security Agency primary sources only; flood warnings, flood-map planning, surface-water, severe-weather warning and weather-health alert methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Weather-health alert partnership
verified_claims: Weather-health alerts are issued by UKHSA in partnership with the Met Office.
limitations: A joint alert is a population-health warning and not a clinical record for an individual.

sources.name: Adverse-temperature health-warning purpose
verified_claims: The system monitors hot and cold episodes that may affect health and issues an appropriate alert after assessment.
limitations: A forecast health impact does not prove morbidity or mortality at a named location.

sources.name: Heat and cold alert components
verified_claims: The system includes Heat-Health Alerts and Cold-Health Alerts.
limitations: The two components must not be combined without preserving season and hazard type.

sources.name: Heat-health core season
verified_claims: The Heat-Health Alert core season operates from 1 June to 30 September.
limitations: Core-season dates do not prevent exceptional alerts outside the season.

sources.name: Cold-health core season in 2026 user guide
verified_claims: The April 2026 user guide states that the Cold-Health Alert season operates from 1 November to 30 March.
limitations: Season-end wording should be versioned because other landing-page text may use a different end-date convention.

sources.name: Out-of-season weather-health alerts
verified_claims: An out-of-season heat or cold alert may be issued when health impacts are expected.
limitations: Absence of a core-season alert does not prove absence of weather-related health risk.

sources.name: Joint dynamic risk assessment
verified_claims: UKHSA and the Met Office conduct a joint dynamic risk assessment when forecast hot or cold episodes meet predefined considerations.
limitations: The assessment is dynamic and must not be represented as a static parcel score.

sources.name: Evidence-based alert considerations
verified_claims: Alert decisions use predefined evidence-based considerations alongside weather forecasts.
limitations: The publication does not expose a parcel-level deterministic threshold for every alert decision.

sources.name: Regional alert subscription
verified_claims: Registered users can select the government region for which they receive alerts.
limitations: Government-region targeting is much coarser than parcel geography.

sources.name: Alert response communication chain
verified_claims: Alert levels trigger communication of risk to NHS England, government and the public-health system.
limitations: Communication activation does not establish realised health outcomes.

sources.name: Alert advice audiences
verified_claims: After an alert is issued or updated, advice is sent to the public and health and social-care professionals, especially those supporting at-risk groups.
limitations: Advice distribution is a preparedness action rather than evidence of individual exposure.

sources.name: Weather-health and severe-weather system separation
verified_claims: UKHSA Weather-Health Alerts are separate from the Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service and focus specifically on health impacts.
limitations: The two systems must not be deduplicated solely because they reference the same weather episode.

sources.name: Adverse Weather and Health Plan purpose
verified_claims: The Adverse Weather and Health Plan aims to protect individuals and communities from health effects of adverse weather and build resilience.
limitations: The plan is a preparedness framework and not evidence that a local organisation has implemented every action.

sources.name: Adverse-weather health outcome aims
verified_claims: The plan seeks to prevent additional mortality and morbidity, reduce years of life lost and reduce healthcare use caused by adverse weather.
limitations: Programme aims are not measured outcome values for a specific event or locality.

sources.name: Adverse-weather planning action areas
verified_claims: The plan identifies nine action areas including service delivery, capacity, organisational arrangements, communication, risk management, early warning, research, quality assurance and accountability.
limitations: The action-area list is a planning framework and not a compliance score for an organisation.
